correctness.rationale: The proof gives a lattice isomorphism and exact facet inequalities via a convex mixture; active Q facets form Boolean subcubes. Their only minimal dependent configurations are a 4-Q square, 2-Q plus 2-zero flip, or total/choice/complementary-zero group. Each has an explicit primitive circuit in a saturated lattice; all other cones extend to integral bases. The torus quotient invariant rings give A1 threefold conifolds or 2-by-m rank-one determinantal cones, with the advertised multiplicities and Q-Gorenstein criterion. Direct exact Python enumerations agree for m=2,3,4, and minor-gcd unimodularity checks for m=2,3, but generality is furnished by the symbolic proof, not experiments.

originality.rationale: Ohsugi--Hibi (arXiv:0804.4287, full paper, Theorem 1.8) gives a global simplicity criterion, not the full reduced singular-orbit-closure decomposition and generic transverse models for all triangle windmills. Tran--Ziegler (DOI:10.37236/3633, Theorem 19 and Section 5) studies general facets and K4-blade windmills, but not this K3-blade singular stratification. Earlier own research treats local fixed-point charts for the same family or the two-triangle special case only. Actual published-finding corpus searches by aliases, graph, local toric models and formulas returned no dominating or equivalent claim; absence of a match is not novelty proof. Residual risk of unindexed formulations remains.

value.rationale: A complete reduced singular-locus classification for an all-parameter natural graph-toric family identifies three separate irreducible-component families, exact exponential counts, two distinct types of generic transverse singularities and a sharp Q-Gorenstein transition. It is not merely a global simplicity test or a local single-chart computation; generic Segre components and codimension-three conifold components have different dimensions for every m>=3.
